criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Per frame: 01 6.5, 02 5.0, 03 7.0, 04 7.0, 05 5.5, 06 5.5, 07 7.0, 08 5.0, 09 6.5. Strong frames: 04, where the 19-disc brass macro stands on true black with lit chamfers; 07, a bold blued stack over a glowing brass pan; and 03, where all 39 wells count at feed size (19/15/1/4, rows checked) and the empty wells read as missing. Four frames fall well short of THE SHOWSTOPPER TEST. 08: the bottom 45 percent is streaky procedural orange wood in the mid tones, the back wall is a flat navy that reads as sky rather than a room, no window is in frame, the storyboard's nameplates are absent and the shut case reads as a laptop. 02: the top 45 percent is empty black. A hard step seam runs at display y about 1000, with a step at x 800 (native about 1350 and 1080). The lit grey sheet is a mid band and the slotted weight reads as a Q-shaped coin. 05: a grey board scored with vector-looking Voronoi hairlines, plus a rectangular notch artifact top left (native about x 0 to 1080, y 1190 to 1350), the same seam as 02. It reads as a UI progress bar, not a lit relief. 06: the planned macro failed and 01's camera was reused. The needle is a flat grey plank, the arc is dark mush whose graduations you can't read at feed size, and a DOM leader and white dot do the reading the render should do. Cropped stacks poke into both bottom corners by the footer. The two weight models also differ: knurled coin stacks on 01/04/07/09, flat Q-slot discs on 02/03/05. On 04 and 07 the knurl reads as barcode bars on the shadow side, and the blued metal reads lilac. Several frames lean on defaults, so this sits below the 7 descriptor.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: Real spine. One brass balance with the 19/15 load recurs on 01, 04, 06, 07 and 09. Brass and blued keep one meaning throughout, and every cast runs right from a left key. The motif evolution is legible from loaded, to counted, to laid in rows, to shut. But three frames step out of the world rather than one. 02 is a grey document plan, 05 a grey clay diagram, and both carry the same tile seam. 08 is a warm orange room with no weight in it. The value track strobes there; the flow summary itself says VALUE_ARC is 'declared rather than delivered'. The arc is pale tan on 01 and dark brown on 06 and 09, and the weight model changes between spatial and relief frames.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces in figures.json: 190,000 (c1), 150,000 (c2), 10,000 (c3), 40,000 and 390,000 (c4), 49 percent (chatgpt_pct_of_ceiling), 79 cents (darwin_cents_per_chat_dollar), 133 cents (ceiling_cents_per_resident), 293,286 (c15), and 39/19/15/1/4 (units). Every source is primary: Legistar API, darwingov.com and Census. 'Approved' is held to the draft minutes on 08 and in the caption, and Darwin's claims are attributed and quoted verbatim on 07 (c9, c10 match). One loose phrasing: 03's hook 'The whole bill, in weights' calls a not-to-exceed ceiling with a $40,000 unspent reserve a bill. Lead for the integrity judge: art_preflight.json lists needs_review: [9] even though the frame 9 hashes in review and frame_inputs match. Worth confirming that the close's review is current.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: Who (Plano City Council), what (four lines, $390,000 ceiling), when (October 12th) and how (consent agenda, one motion, draft minutes) are all clear and accurate. Collin and Denton appear only as hashtags. Nothing tells a Texan what they can still do: the draft minutes come up for approval, or they could ask the council how the licenses will be used. The stake is stated generally, closing on a question in the caption.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover's two-pan image earns the swipe, 02 pays at once (one motion), and 05 is a declared turn. 03 and 04 overlap, since 04 restates 03's brass count as a percent. 06's 'difference equals the reserve' is an arithmetic coincidence and the most cuttable frame. The close, 'about 133 cents a resident', lands softly rather than hard.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register, and the house rules hold: no colons, no banned words, ordinal dates. Two hooks are stilted: 04 'Of the ceiling, 49 percent covers the chatbot' and 09 'A ceiling of about 133 cents a resident', where any Texan would say a dollar thirty-three. Texas texture is thin beyond the name Plano. The Blackland clay and Austin chalk live only in the storyboard, not in anything a reader sees.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: A fresh concept against no. 60 (yard), no. 61 (drone and dock) and no. 62 (towers): a tabletop instrument in brass and blued steel, plus a weight case and reliefs. The familiar moves are the lastLight navy staged sky with type stacked top-left over an object on a plinth, the same opening move as recent covers.

one_sentence_fix: Rebuild the three frames that leave the instrument's world (02's grey agenda plan, 05's grey clay diagram, 08's orange dais) as staged lastLight renders of the same brass weights in one pool on a dark field, and delete the half-width wash seam that 02 and 05 share, because those three frames hold down both artwork_craft and deck_coherence.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Bottom 45 percent is mid-tone orange procedural wood. The back wall is flat navy that reads as sky, not a room. No window is in frame, the nameplates are missing and the shut case reads as a laptop, so the frame fails 'a room is dark around one source'.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Push the camera in to ledge height (eye 0.9 m, fov 30) so the case fills a third of the width, kill the room fill so the dais front falls to near black, and light only a narrow window shaft from the left across the lid and brass latch, with the window frame visible top left.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Top 45 percent is dead black over a hard step seam (native about y 1350, step at x 1080). The pooled grey sheet is a flat mid band and the weight reads as a Q-shaped coin.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Re-shoot as an oblique txthree view at elevation 13 so the agenda leaf recedes into the dark, with the pool only on row (f) and the knurled stack-style weight standing on it. Remove the wash/tile seam so the board falls off continuously.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A grey board with vector-looking Voronoi hairlines and a rectangular notch artifact (native about x 0 to 1080, y 1190 to 1350) reads as a UI progress bar. The discs barely stand proud.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lay the two rows in grooves on the dark chalk plinth at a low three-quarter txthree camera, with the key raking along the grooves so each disc casts. Extend the board's falloff across the full width to remove the notch.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: 01's camera repeated. The needle renders as a flat grey plank, the dark arc's graduations are unreadable, and a DOM leader and white dot carry the reading.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Build the planned macro with the pillar moved out of frame to the left: camera level with the arc at 0.30 m, a nickel BRDF on the needle with the key down its bevel, and a lit brass index under the tip. Then drop the DOM dot and leader.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The balance is a thin linework silhouette with little mass. The plinth face is a flat taupe band under the source line, the needle is the same grey plank, and the chamber glazing is cool navy, so the declared warm seam is absent.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move the camera to 1.0 m at fov 24 so the beam spans about 80 percent of the width and the stacks gain mass, warm the city hall glazing into a seam behind the beam, and let the plinth face fall out of the pool to black.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The knurl reads as barcode bars on the shadow side, and the headline sits on a darkening wash plate over the flat taupe plinth.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Replace the knurl geometry with a fine normal map so the shadow side falls to black, and drop the plinth out of the key pool so the type sits on true dark without a plate.
